subject: Comparing models (re-running models) across many datasets

messages.author: 6c4d187713e325b8
messages.subject: Comparing models (re-running models) across many datasets
parts:
Hey all,
      I am hoping to write a loop function that will re-run a model in Lavaan based on a grouping variable (here I am using CFA).  e.g., If I have the data from 10 studies in a single dataset (with a factor variable to indicate which rows belong to which studies), I would like to re-run the model for each study then return a table with all the fit indicies. This would also be useful to run models by any subset of the data, e.g., sex, age, etc.

To do this, I have combined all the data into one dataset called "data" and created a variable "Study" which indicates which study the results belong to. Then I am splitting the data by this factor (using the split function), running the model on each object in the list, and extracting the fit indicies of interest (simplifying them by sapply). 

I imagine the solution lies in the "apply" loop where the "data"  in the cfa(model, data) is currently a list containing the split data. The function needs to change this (data = Splitdata) to the current value of "i" in the list (Splitdata) that is being looped. 

The final line of code that extracts the fits seems to be working fine. 

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
I have called the data "data", and the grouping variable "Study". 

# First we specify the model
Model      <- ' Factor1 =~ var.1 + var.2 + var.3 + var.4
                      Factor 2 =~ var.5 + var.6 + var.7 + var.8 '

# then split the data into a list containing each study's data
Splitdata <- split(data, data$Study)

#Now create a new list containing each model
Cfa.Models <- apply(Splitdata, function(Splitdata) cfa(model, data = Splitdata)) 

#Finally, we can pull out the desired fit indicies

Cfa.Fits <- sapply(Cfa.Models, function(Cfa.Models) fitMeasures(Cfa.Models, c("chisq", "df","fmin", "cfi", "nnfi", "srmr", "rmsea", "rmsea.ci.lower", "rmsea.ci.upper", "rmsea.pvalue") )) 

             Error in match.fun(FUN) : argument "FUN" is missing, with no default

---------------------------------------------------------------------------


Thanks for all of your help with this problem!!!! 
            -  Conal

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Comparing models (re-running models) across many datasets
parts:
apply() applies a function along a particular dimension of a matrix/array, and it's second argument is which dimension (1 = rows, 2 = columns), not the function (which should be the third argument).  Instead, use lapply(), which should work without changing anything else.

Terry

parts:
Thank you very much for your help. lapply (or sapply) does help to rerun the model along the list. However, the Lavaan component (  cfa(model, data = Splitdata)   ) will not run as it requires a matrix/data.frame and not a list. We need to find a way to tell Lavaan to take the current matrix in the list as the data = "data" (such as telling Lavaan to define the current dataset in the list as a particular object which is included in the data section. Then, as each iteration runs it will then re-define the object and input it into this section).

messages.subject: Re: Comparing models (re-running models) across many datasets
parts:
For all those looking to replicate this, I think I have cracked it (see below).  I have also added a similar function on the end to add power to the table. This will work for any grouping factor.

Note, I simply ran the model once and took the degrees of freedom which I inputted into the findRMSEApower() function.

Cfa.Models <- lapply(Splitdata, function(x) cfa(Model, data = as.data.frame(x)))
Cfa.Fits <- sapply(Cfa.Models, function(y) fitMeasures(y, c("chisq", "df","fmin", "cfi", "nnfi", "srmr", "rmsea", "rmsea.ci.lower", "rmsea.ci.upper", "rmsea.pvalue") ))            
Cfa.ss <-  lapply(Splitdata, function(z) N = nrow(z))
                Cfa.powers <-  sapply(Cfa.ss, function(p)
                               findRMSEApower(rmsea0=.080, rmseaA=.060, df=33, n = p))
Models <- rbind(Cfa.Fits, Cfa.powers)
